newsitem.title: USA: Three Georgia counties approve sales tax proposals.
newsitem.headline: Three Georgia counties approve sales tax proposals.

text.p: Voters in three Georgia counties approved one-cent local option sales taxes, elections officials said Wednesday.
In Henry county, the sales tax will rise to 6 percent from 5 percent, raising $60 million over five years for roads, libraries, senior centers and recreation.

In Coweta County, voters approved a five-year extension that will keep the sales tax at 6 percent, raising $46 million for roads and bridges. The tax had been set to expire on Dec 31. The county will receive about two-thirds of the added revenue, with the rest divided among its seven municipalities. Tift County voters also agreed to extend
their sales tax by five years, keeping it at 6 percent. That will raise about $16 milion for airport, landfill, road and sewer projects. The tax had been set to expire on Sept 30.
All three sales tax proposals passed in elections Tuesday.
